conclusions: Current episode save reads its station before prepareContentRelations reads the program. Program transfer initially reads program before reading station counters. This sequence exists at pre-B13 baseline c304e85.
B13 did not change editorial-audit.js or introduce the existing transfer scenario. RSS fixtures have unique program/station/episode IDs, scoped queries, and no clearing.

Firestore uses shared read locks and exclusive write locks. A reversed pair of read orders alone does not demonstrate a deadlock; both operations later update the program and may legitimately contend.
A mock using exclusive locks for transactional reads would not model documented Firestore semantics and cannot provide valid business RED.

No deterministic failing business assertion establishing a read-order correction has been demonstrated. No speculative application source patch, retry increase, test serialization, assertion relaxation or emulator launch was performed.
The diagnostic rerun provides a passing integration gate but does not resolve or explain the original instability. Independent review and retained instability obligation remain necessary.
